description: You are a backend engineer at a high-traffic e-commerce platform. The inventory-service project at /home/ga/inventory-service is experiencing data corruption under concurrent load during peak sales events — stock levels go negative, reservations are double-booked, and counters are consistently wrong. Import the project into Eclipse. Your task is to identify ALL thread-safety violations in the codebase and fix them using appropriate java.util.concurrent primitives. Specifically: StockCounter uses plain int fields that are not thread-safe under concurrent increment; ProductCatalog uses HashMap which can corrupt under concurrent reads/writes; InventoryManager has both a non-thread-safe HashMap and a check-then-act race condition in removeStock(); ReservationService lacks synchronization on compound multi-map operations. Fix all four components. After fixing, add JUnit 5 tests that verify thread safety using multiple concurrent threads (using ExecutorService or Thread), and run 'mvn clean test' to confirm all tests pass.

metadata.bug_1: StockCounter — plain int fields need AtomicInteger
metadata.bug_3: InventoryManager — HashMap + non-atomic check-then-act in removeStock()
metadata.bug_4: ReservationService — unsynchronized compound operations on two maps
